issues.legal_issue: A tenant who has attorned to a landlord and paid rent to that person may be estopped from denying that person’s title, including when a successor claims through that landlord.
material_facts: The tenant attorned to the purchaser and paid rent to him.
When a later purchaser claimed through that landlord, the tenant denied the title on the basis that the landlord’s own vendor had lacked title.
The tenant did not establish that his attornment resulted from mistake or misrepresentation.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was precluded by the general principles of estoppel between landlord and tenant from denying the title of the landlord to whom he had attorned, and could not defeat the successor’s derivative title on the asserted basis.
issues.legal_principle: Section 116 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, embodies but does not exhaust the law of estoppel between landlord and tenant. Although it concerns denial of the landlord’s title at the beginning of the tenancy, estoppel may also arise outside the section when a tenant attorns to another and accepts that person as landlord, including by paying rent. The tenant may avoid such estoppel by establishing that the attornment resulted from mistake or ignorance of material facts, particularly where caused by fraud. The Court relied on Kumar Krishna Prasad Lal Singha Deo v. Baraboni Coal Concern Ltd., AIR 1937 PC 251, for the distinction between Section 116 estoppel and other estoppels arising between landlord and tenant.

rule.if: tenancy_title_dispute and tenant_attorned_to_claimant and tenant_paid_rent_to_claimant and successor_claims_through_attorned_landlord and challenge_depends_on_attorned_landlords_lack_of_title and not attornment_proven_mistaken_or_fraudulent

predicates.tenancy_title_dispute: The proceeding concerns a tenant’s challenge to the title of a person claiming as landlord.
predicates.tenant_attorned_to_claimant: The tenant expressly or by conduct recognized the claimant as landlord.
predicates.tenant_paid_rent_to_claimant: The tenant paid rent to the person he had recognized as landlord.
predicates.successor_claims_through_attorned_landlo: A successor claims the landlord’s interest through the person to whom the tenant attorned.
predicates.challenge_depends_on_attorned_landlords_: The tenant’s challenge to the successor’s title rests on an assertion that the attorned landlord lacked title.
predicates.attornment_proven_mistaken_or_fraudulent: The tenant established that the attornment resulted from mistake, ignorance of material facts, or fraud.

issues.definition: When a tenant in a title dispute attorns to a claimant, pays rent to that claimant, and a successor claims through that claimant, the tenant is estopped from denying the attorned landlord’s title if the tenant has not shown that the attornment was mistaken or fraudulent.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s denial of the landlord’s title can constitute a ground for eviction even if the tenant has not renounced the tenant’s status.
material_facts: The tenant denied the landlord’s title by asserting that the landlord’s vendor had no title to convey.
The tenant’s denial was the basis of the ejectment proceedings.
The landlord’s right to rely on the denial had not been waived or the tenant’s conduct condoned.
issues.conclusion: The tenant’s conduct amounted to a denial of the landlord’s title and attracted the statutory ground for eviction, even without renunciation of the tenant’s character.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(1)(f) of the Uttar Pradesh (Temporary) Control of Rent and Eviction Act, 1947, provides a ground for eviction where a tenant renounces the tenant’s character or denies the landlord’s title, provided the landlord has not waived the right or condoned the conduct. These are alternative grounds: a tenant can deny title without renouncing the tenant’s status, as where the tenant sets up a jus tertii. The Court applied the general principles of estoppel between landlord and tenant to conclude that the denial in this case was impermissible.

predicates.rent_control_ejectment_proceeding: The proceeding seeks eviction of a tenant under a rent-control regime.
predicates.tenant_denied_landlords_title: The tenant asserted that the person claiming as landlord lacked title.
predicates.landlord_right_not_waived_or_conduct_not: The landlord did not waive reliance on the denial or condone the tenant’s conduct.

issues.definition: In a rent-control eviction proceeding, a tenant’s denial of the landlord’s title satisfies the eviction ground when the landlord has not waived or condoned that conduct, even if the tenant has not renounced the tenant’s status.
